A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain 17 readable pages, including Appendices A–J. Text and rendered-page comparison establish that the scientific content is identical; differences are confined to the title page and bibliography.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation experiments and 262 real-robot navigation episodes, including agent comparisons, memory ablations, and dynamics and occupancy probing results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original simulation and real-robot results, including the comparisons in Figure 3, probing results in Figures 7 and 9, and appendix Table 5.

M1.justification: The PPO/GRU navigation agent, RMA-inspired adaptation, and dynamics and occupancy probing procedures are unchanged, including their architecture and training descriptions in the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same HM3D data and real/scanned test building for point-goal navigation. Dynamics-corruption scenarios, crowded navigation, and appendix evaluations retain identical coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: D4, D28-instant and D28-dynamics in Figure 3 and Table 5; the probing variants in Figure 7; and R2D2 versus AMCL in Table 4.

E3.justification: Evaluation splits, episode counts, SR/SPL/SCT metrics, success thresholds and experimental controls are identical. Both retain 500-million-step PPO training and the same probing split, horizon and optimization settings in Appendices D and J.

E4.justification: Dynamics and odometry perturbations, speed and delay tests, memory ablations, Shapley analysis, planning heatmaps and the tunnel-vision case study are retained without revision, including supplementary analyses in the appendices.

E5.justification: Figure 3 retains mean and standard deviation reporting across four real-robot evaluations of 20 episodes each. Run information and uncertainty displays elsewhere are also unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match, including the real-robot success rate of 92.5 ± 2.9 in Figure 3, probing errors in Figure 7, and training-domain results in appendix Table 5.

T1.justification: The distance-to-belief definition, dynamical equations, probing losses and planning cost function are identical, including Equations 4–11 in Appendices B–F. No mathematical reasoning or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about learned dynamics, prediction/correction behavior, encoded scene information and limited-horizon planning. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations remain identical, including reliance on odometry, evidence for short-to-medium-horizon plans, and the failure to establish correct long-term plans discussed in Section 8 and Appendix H.

D1.justification: Hardware, architecture, hyperparameters, visual-localization procedures and probing implementation details are unchanged. The embedded project-resource links also have identical targets.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 83 numbered reference entries and identical research positioning. Expanded venue names and bibliographic metadata edits do not introduce or remove cited works.

P1.justification: v4 changes Francesco Giuliari's affiliation from IIT to Fondazione Bruno Kessler and expands many bibliography venue names. It also introduces reference typos, including 'Intenational' and 'P0ion' in reference [34]. The scientific prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The additional affiliation slightly shifts first-page text, and expanded references reflow across pages 9–11. Figures 1–15 and Tables 1–5 retain their content and presentation; all appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v4 preserves the complete scientific argument, empirical evidence, limitations and reproducibility information. The affiliation update and expanded reference presentation are editorial changes, accompanied by minor bibliographic typos. Their benefits and drawbacks are too limited to meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
